description: Make session context-health a proactive, surface-consistent signal: alert treatment on the shared indicator, sticky recovery bar, persisted compaction lineage with a navigable link, a compact compaction summary atop the transcript, and a context-usage trend mini-chart backed by a short retained usage history.

tasks.title: Server: persist runtime-session lineage chain
tasks.description: In the Agent/Sessions domain, record an ordered RuntimeSessionLineage chain on AgentSessionStatusSnapshot (entries { AgentRuntimeSessionId, BoundAt }). Update RebindRuntimeSession to append a new entry on each rebind so the predecessor runtime-session id (currently discarded in AgentSession.Transitions.cs) is retained. Extend the AgentSessionRuntimeBound event with PreviousAgentRuntimeSessionId so the transition stays event-sourced/observable. Project the lineage (or derived previous/next for the current runtime session) onto AgentSessionMetadataDto via the existing querier mapping, keeping the fields optional. This is the authoritative source of truth the Web will read; do not reconstruct lineage client-side.
acceptanceCriteria: AgentSessionStatusSnapshot carries an ordered RuntimeSessionLineage that starts with one entry and grows on each compact/reset rebind.
RebindRuntimeSession appends the new runtime-session entry while retaining all prior entries (predecessor no longer overwritten/lost).
AgentSessionRuntimeBound event carries PreviousAgentRuntimeSessionId for realtime consumers.
AgentSessionMetadataDto exposes the lineage relationship (nullable/optional), projected by the existing grain/querier path.
Historical sessions (compacted before this change) render no lineage / single-entry chain without error (no backfill required).
`npm test` (server) passes; grain-level Fake tests assert: initial single entry, append-on-rebind retains predecessor, DTO projection reflects the chain.
tasks.output: packages/server AgentSession state/event/DTO extensions + passing server tests (dotnet build treat-warnings-as-errors + npm test)
tasks.notes: Keys lineage off the stable Mohist sessionId; the chain is a sequence of mutable AgentRuntimeSessionId facets (conventions.md identity rule). Forward-only, no compatibility obligation.

tasks.title: Server: retain bounded context-usage history
tasks.description: Retain a short, bounded ContextUsageHistory on AgentSession.Status (e.g. List<{ At, Percent }>), appended on usage.updated/context_health_update and hard-capped + time-thinned (target ~24 samples, coarse time bucketing) so grain state and payloads stay small. Expose the history by enriching the existing ActivityCardDto.Usage with the history list — this is the only permitted relaxation of the Pulse 'no new endpoint' constraint; add NO new query route. Keep fields nullable/optional.
acceptanceCriteria: AgentSession.Status retains a ContextUsageHistory list that is appended on usage updates.
The history is hard-capped and time-thinned so it cannot grow unbounded regardless of session length (bounded payload).
ActivityCardDto.Usage carries the usage history; no independent new backend query endpoint is introduced.
Sessions with no recorded usage expose an empty/absent history without error.
`npm test` (server) passes; Fake tests assert: cap is enforced (last-N retained), time-thinning coalesces nearby samples, and the activity DTO maps the history through the existing querier.
tasks.output: packages/server AgentSession usage-history state + ActivityCardDto.Usage enrichment + passing server tests
tasks.notes: Honors 'data model as simple as possible'. Server is the source of truth so a freshly-opened Pulse sees a full lifetime trend, not just the latest snapshot.

tasks.title: Web: ContextHealthIndicator alert treatment
tasks.description: Enhance the shared ContextHealthIndicator (packages/web/src/widgets/session-health/ui/ContextHealthIndicator.tsx) so yellow (60-79.99%) and red (>=80%) render an explicit alert treatment: alert color plus a warning/error glyph, role/aria (role="alert" + aria-live="polite" for red, role="status" for yellow), and a descriptive severity tooltip (e.g. 'Context window 82% full — near limit') instead of a bare percentage. Reuse the existing classifyContextHealth/resolveContextHealth classifier unchanged. Green stays quiet (no alert styling); missing/non-finite data hides the indicator entirely. Because SessionCard, CompactSessionCard, and the session page all route through this one component, the treatment is consistent by construction — do not add per-call-site alert logic.
acceptanceCriteria: Yellow threshold renders yellow alert color + warning glyph + role="status" + descriptive tooltip.
Red threshold renders red alert color + error glyph + role="alert" + aria-live="polite" + descriptive tooltip.
Green (<60%) renders without any alert styling or warning color (quiet).
Missing/non-finite/non-positive-window data renders nothing (no misleading empty/zero indicator).
The same usage percentage produces identical alert color + tooltip behavior across SessionCard list rows, Pulse CompactSessionCard, and the session page.

`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass; component tests cover all four threshold scenarios plus the cross-surface consistency scenario (use Fakes for the activity/session sources).
tasks.notes: Pure presentation change; classifier logic is reused unchanged. No server dependency — the latest-snapshot data already exists.

tasks.title: Web: sticky recovery bar in SessionPage
tasks.description: Make the recovery-bar sub-region of SessionHeader sticky within the page scroll context (SessionPage.tsx ~565-569), with a background and z-index above the transcript, so the context-health bar and the SessionRecoveryActions Compact/Reset buttons stay reachable while the transcript body scrolls. Pin only the recovery sub-region — do NOT pin the entire header (breadcrumb/title need not be pinned) and do NOT introduce a floating FAB. Keep the existing active||pending disable on Compact/Reset unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: The recovery-bar sub-region remains visible (sticky) while the transcript body is scrolled, independent of viewport height.
The context-health bar and the Compact/Reset actions remain reachable without scrolling back to the top.
Only the recovery sub-region is pinned; the breadcrumb/title header is not forced sticky.
The active||pending disable behavior on Compact/Reset buttons is unchanged.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass; a scroll-stick test asserts the recovery bar stays visible after the transcript scrolls.
tasks.output: SessionPage sticky recovery region + web typecheck/test passing
tasks.notes: Pure layout/CSS change, no server dependency. Keeps the pinned region compact to mitigate short-viewport space loss.

tasks.title: Web: CompactionCompactSummary atop the transcript
tasks.description: Add a CompactionCompactSummary component in the session-health widget that renders a one-line aggregate of all of the session's compaction events (count, times, strategies, aggregate token reduction), fed by the same compaction-event list already available to the transcript model. Place it atop the transcript body (coder-session SessionTimeline / session transcript) so it is visible without expanding any individual round. Hide the summary when there are zero compaction events. Keep the existing per-round CompactionTimelineEntry (SessionTimeline.tsx ~303) intact for detailed before/after token counts and summary.
acceptanceCriteria: A session with one or more compaction events renders a compact summary visible without expanding any transcript round.
The summary surfaces compaction count/times/strategies and aggregate token reduction.
The per-round CompactionTimelineEntry remains available for detailed before/after token counts.
A session with zero compaction events renders no compact summary.

`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass; tests assert summary renders from compaction events and stays hidden when there are none (Fakes for event/session sources).
tasks.output: CompactionCompactSummary component + transcript wiring + web typecheck/test passing
tasks.notes: Uses existing compaction-event data; no server change required. Avoids duplicating the in-round detail by composing a dedicated aggregate summary atop the transcript.

tasks.title: Web: CompactionLineageLink navigation between runtime sessions
tasks.description: Add a CompactionLineageLink component in the session-health widget that reads the RuntimeSessionLineage exposed by AgentSessionMetadataDto (T-001) and renders a navigable link to the predecessor runtime session (common case, page shows latest) and, for completeness, to a successor when a non-latest runtime session is in view. Because runtime sessions of one Mohist session share one URL, implement navigation via a ?rt=<runtimeSessionId> query param that anchors the transcript to the compaction boundary for that runtime session — do not invent a new per-runtime-session route. Wire the link into the sticky recovery region (T-004). Render nothing when the chain has a single entry (no compaction relationship).
acceptanceCriteria: A runtime session compacted/reset into a successor renders a lineage link to that successor; activating it navigates to the successor runtime session.
A runtime session produced from a predecessor renders a lineage link back to it; activating it navigates to the predecessor runtime session.
A runtime session with no compaction predecessor or successor (single-entry chain) renders no lineage link.
Activating a link uses the ?rt=<runtimeSessionId> anchor scheme within the existing session route (no new route added).
The link is placed within the recovery region and degrades to hidden when lineage data is absent (historical sessions).
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass; tests cover predecessor, successor, and no-link scenarios using Fakes for the session/lineage source.
tasks.output: CompactionLineageLink component + session-page wiring + web typecheck/test passing
tasks.notes: Depends on T-001 for the lineage DTO fields and T-004 for the sticky recovery region it is rendered within (avoids conflicting edits to the same SessionPage region). Stable identity remains the Mohist sessionId.

tasks.title: Web: ContextUsageTrendMiniChart on Pulse compact cards
tasks.description: Add a ContextUsageTrendMiniChart component (lightweight inline SVG sparkline, no charting dependency) in the session-health widget. Map the usage history exposed by ActivityCardDto.Usage (T-002) into the card model in activity-cards.ts and render the mini-chart on CompactSessionCard (dashboard-pulse) so the card shows a context-usage trend over the session lifetime rather than only the latest snapshot. The chart degrades gracefully — hide it when there are fewer than 2 samples — rather than rendering a broken or empty-axis chart. Keep the Pulse zone read-only; no new endpoint and no domain writes.
acceptanceCriteria: A compact card for a session with a non-empty usage history renders a context-usage trend mini-chart derived from that history.
A compact card for a session with no usage history or fewer than 2 samples degrades gracefully (chart hidden, no broken/empty-axis chart rendered).
activity-cards.ts maps the enriched ActivityCardDto.Usage history into the card model without adding a new backend endpoint or any write operation.
The Pulse zone remains purely read-only with respect to domain state.

`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass; tests assert the chart renders from history and degrades to hidden when history is empty/insufficient (Fakes for the activity source).
tasks.output: ContextUsageTrendMiniChart component + activity-cards mapping + CompactSessionCard rendering + web typecheck/test passing
tasks.notes: Depends on T-002 for the usage-history enrichment of ActivityCardDto.Usage. Inline SVG only — do not introduce a charting library dependency.
